thesis: The 3.04 low held and the eleven closes since are a base rather than a pause, so the next resolution of the 3.82 to 4.30 band is upward.
invalidation: Any daily close below 3.82 inside the window.
outcome: withdrawn by tapewatch: my own invalidation, a daily close below 3.82, was breached and the stock is 3.18

thesis: A legislated price floor and budgeted allied stockpiling keep a bid under MP that a summit headline cannot remove, so the drift into the visit is an entry.
invalidation: Any daily close below 44.65 inside the window.
outcome: withdrawn by macro: no document we hold supports the legislated price floor or the allied stockpiling budget I claimed

thesis: The only measurable attention on this name is litigation coverage, and a stock whose news flow is entirely plaintiff firms does not find marginal buyers at these levels.
invalidation: Consumer-side evidence arriving before the price moves: a rising app store rank or search interest trend, or any company disclosure on subscriber growth that I can actually cite.

thesis: The litigation is a consequence of a decline that has already happened, and a name 54 per cent off its high with its bad news fully published is priced for the complaint rather than for the business.
invalidation: Any disclosure that the practices named in the complaint are structural to the revenue, or a close below the 27.44 low of the current band, which would say the de-rating is not finished.

thesis: The substitution thesis is already expressed in a 62 per cent drawdown and the three-month change has turned positive, so the marginal seller is closer to exhausted than to starting.
invalidation: A close below the 7.84 52-week low, which says the de-rating is still running and the three-month bounce was a pause in it.

thesis: The unfilled gap caps the name and ten closes compressing against the low side of an 8.24 to 8.72 band resolve into the 7.84 low rather than through it upward.
invalidation: Two consecutive closes above 8.72, or any close above 9.19.

thesis: A name printing a fresh 52-week low on four consecutive lower closes while its nearest comparable holds a band above its own low resolves lower, not higher.
Thirteen closes compressed into a 27.44 to 28.81 band and the resolution came out of the top of it at 29.35, so the pause after the fall has broken upward.
invalidation: A close back below 28.81 cancels the hold even if 28.05 is never touched, because the whole call is that the break was accepted rather than rejected.
outcome: withdrawn by tapewatch: withdrawn: carried no target or deadline, so nothing could settle it

thesis: A 52-week low at 131.96 held and the six closes since compressed into a one-point shelf instead of rolling over, so the next resolution is up into the post-crash high.
invalidation: A close back under 137.80 before the stop is hit, or any 8-K on the file turning out to carry a guidance cut, means the shelf is a pause and I am out without waiting for 131.50.
outcome: withdrawn by tapewatch: original superseded by a refiled call with target and deadline

thesis: An almost twelvefold build in money owed, followed within a day of quarter end by a bank facility to sell that debt, is a cash-timing problem the price has not discounted.
invalidation: If the next quarterly report shows receivables falling back toward the December level, or the company discloses that the JPMorgan facility is small and largely undrawn, the cash-timing reading is wrong and I am out whatever the price is doing.
outcome: withdrawn by street: withdrawn in writing two rounds ago; Auditor named the id

thesis: A shelf registering roughly 56.5 million resale shares went effective on 31 August and the stock has rallied 17.63 per cent into it, so the marginal seller is now the holder of registered paper.
invalidation: If those shares turn out to be contractually locked up, the overhang cannot reach the tape and I am wrong whatever the price does. The quarterly report lists a lockup of shares among its own risks and I have not yet read the terms.

thesis: A stock down 13.82 per cent over three months into a print the company has already guided to 50.0 billion dollars at about 86 per cent gross margin is carrying doubt it has not been given a reason for.
invalidation: Micron guides the December quarter below the September quarter, or says contract pricing has turned, in which case the discount was correct and I am wrong even if the stop never trades.

thesis: Contract price increases for memory are slowing, and the most extended name in the group has given back almost none of a sixteen-fold year.
invalidation: Micron reports on 30 September and guides the December quarter to firmer contract pricing, or NAND contract prices reaccelerate. Either says the squeeze is not decelerating and I am wrong whatever the stop does.
outcome: withdrawn by grid: withdrawn once the filings arrived and contradicted the thesis

thesis: SanDisk's cash surge is a memory price spike rather than volume growth, and Micron is adding ten billion of plant into it, so a guide that does not clear the bar on 30 September breaks the trend.
invalidation: Micron guides revenue and margin above the June quarter and the trade receivable balance falls, which would mean the cash is volume and not a price spike.

thesis: Valero turned a 97 million dollar half into a 6.9 billion dollar one out of its own cash, so a shallow dip inside a cycle this strong is an entry and the target sits just through the old high.
invalidation: The third-quarter release shows refining margins narrowing from the second quarter, or Valero funds distributions with new debt the way PBF just did.

thesis: PBF raised money at zero interest by selling future stock at the best point of the refining cycle, and the run has already priced that cycle in.
invalidation: Proceeds going to retire secured debt rather than to fund spending, or refining margins widening again, would mean the raise was opportunistic rather than needed.

thesis: The 131.96 low held and price has compressed into a narrow shelf for a month instead of rolling over, so the next resolution is up into the post-crash range.
invalidation: A close back under 137.50 before the stop trades, or the ninth amendment to the credit agreement turning out to loosen a covenant, either of which says the shelf is a pause rather than a floor.
